Architecture · operators-mcp / coding_pool

How the harness is built

The harness is one Go server that holds the catalog (agents, skills, MCP servers), the work (projects, zones, tickets, documents) and the live agent sessions that act on it. It is built as a hexagonal (ports & adapters) architecture, with its use cases split into DDD bounded contexts and wired at a single composition root. Three clients sit on the same ports: the web UI, the terminal client and the agents themselves through MCP.

01System overview

Who talks to the server, and what the server talks to.

There is one process with several entry points. The server (cmd/server) binds the application services to its inbound adapters. The tui-client (cmd/tui-client) binds HTTP adapters to the same driving port interfaces, so a screen holding a ports.TicketBoard cannot tell whether it is in-process or across the network. Agent sessions are spawned by the server and come back through a session-scoped MCP endpoint, so their tools always act on their own task.

02Layers & the dependency rule

Dependencies point inward. Only the composition root sees every layer.

domain ports application adapters composition root
domain → nothingPure Go types: Project, Zone, Agent, Ticket, Session, Artifact… plus events and errors.
ports → domainInterfaces only, expressed in domain types. No implementation lives here except contract test suites.
application → ports, domainServices depend on driven ports, never on SQLite, git or HTTP packages. Each asserts the driving ports it satisfies at compile time.
adapters → ports, domainInbound adapters call driving ports; outbound adapters implement driven ports.
No context imports anotherContexts read each other through read ports and react to each other through domain events on the bus.
Only internal/app constructsConcrete adapters are chosen once, in fx modules, and bound with fx.As(port).

Driving vs. driven ports

KindDirectionExamples in internal/portsImplemented by
drivingoutside → inOrchestration (= SessionLauncher, SessionControl, SessionReader, SessionStream, SessionFeed, …), Planning, TicketReader, TicketBoardapplication services in the server; adapter/out/httpclient in tui-client
drivenin → outsideTicketRepository, DocumentRepository, ProjectRepository, EventPublisher/EventSubscriber, Shell, PTY, Agent, TerminalHost, ToolRegistryadapter/out/*

03Bounded contexts

Each context is one package under internal/application, with its own service and the language it owns.

Catalog: wired together in internal/app/catalog over one event bus

Projects

application/projects

Projects and the git repositories they are made of, env files, run commands.

  • emits ProjectDeleted

Architecture

application/architecture

How a project's code is carved into zones and bounded contexts; its file tree.

  • reacts ProjectDeleted, AgentDeleted, PromptDeleted

Agents

application/agents

Agent templates and the prompts they are built from. References capabilities by id through CapabilityReader.

  • emits AgentDeleted, PromptDeleted
  • reacts SkillDeleted, MCPServerDeleted

Capabilities

application/capabilities

What an agent can be equipped with: skills, MCP servers, user-defined tools. Core use cases live in harnesskit.

  • emits SkillDeleted, MCPServerDeleted
  • reacts SettingsChanged

Settings

application/settings

Global key/value configuration. Validates and stores; what a change means belongs to the context that owns it.

  • emits SettingsChanged
Work and runtime: separate fx modules

Planning

application/planning

Tickets (tasks on the board) and documents, plus their many-to-many link and document scope (task or project).

  • announces ticket changes on the project feed

Orchestration

application/orchestration

Agent sessions: headless (stream-json) and interactive (terminal). Event hub, project feed, questions and approvals, session modes.

Execution

application/execution

Runs Genkit flows for a zone's agent with scoped tools and context.

Workspaces

application/workspaces

Isolated git worktrees materialised on disk and tracked in the database; repository history.

Apps

application/apps

Runs a repository's application from a session's worktree in a server terminal, keeping its output.

Artifacts

application/artifacts

What a session published to the Design tab: records it, serves the bytes, announces each publish. Nothing is scanned.

Tooling

application/tooling

The registry of built-in tools (filesystem, search/replace, repo map, linter, project/document/context tools) exposed over MCP.

04Patterns in use

What each pattern looks like in this codebase, and where to find it.

PatternHow it shows up hereWhere
Hexagonal / Ports & AdaptersServices see only interfaces; adapters plug in at the edges. The TUI swaps in-process services for HTTP adapters behind the same ports.internal/ports, internal/adapter
Bounded contexts (DDD)One package per context, each with its own service and vocabulary. No context imports another.internal/application/*
Ubiquitous languageProjects, zones, agents, skills, tickets, sessions, artifacts: the same words in the API, CLI, UI copy and code.PRODUCT.md, internal/domain
Domain eventsSmall value types with EventName(): project.deleted, skill.deleted, settings.changed… used only for cross-context side effects.domain/events.go, adapter/out/eventbus
RepositoryOne driven port per aggregate root (TicketRepository, DocumentRepository…), backed by SQLite, with in-memory fakes for tests.ports/*.go, adapter/out/persistence/{sqlite,memory}
Application serviceA Service struct per context holds the use cases, validates, persists through repositories and announces changes.application/*/service.go
Read ports (anti-corruption)A context that needs another's data asks a narrow reader interface (CapabilityReader, TicketReader) instead of its repository.internal/ports
Composition root + DIuber-go/fx modules (PersistenceModule, CatalogModule, PlanningModule, ExecutionModule, ServerModule…) build the graph once.internal/app
Backend for Frontendtempl renders the first paint from driving ports in process; the browser takes over and writes through /api.adapter/in/web, web/
Contract testsThe same suite runs against the service and against its HTTP adapter over the real router; disagreement means the wire is wrong.ports/portstest, ports/runtimetest, web/src/modules/*/testing
Structured errorsEvery failure carries a stable code (SESSION_NOT_FOUND, DOCUMENT_NOT_HTML…) that surfaces unchanged in API, MCP and UI.domain/errors.go (harnesskit errs)
Trade-off worth knowing. The domain is thin: internal/domain holds data structures, events and errors, and most invariants (valid ticket status, same project on link, ordering of announcements) are enforced in the application services. That keeps the layers simple, but a rule added in one service is not automatically enforced in another. When an invariant grows, move it onto the domain type.

06The web client

The same layering repeats in the browser, one module per feature.

web/src/modules/<module>/
  domain/          rules + ports.js — the contracts infrastructure fulfils
  infrastructure/  gateways over /api and SSE, DTO mappers, memory gateway
  presentation/    components, views, register.js (Alpine.data)
  testing/         fixtures, stub API, the port's contract suite
SSR first paintThe Go BFF (adapter/in/web) renders the page and embeds a seed; the module hydrates from it.
Writes go to /apiPages only render; mutations travel from the browser to the REST API, and changes come back over SSE.
Layer rulesdomain imports nothing outward; presentation never imports infrastructure; modules never import each other.
One constructorOnly main.js and dev/main.js construct infrastructure.

07A request, end to end

Moving a ticket to review from an agent session, through every layer.

  1. Agent calls an MCP toolThe session's claude CLI calls update_task_status on /mcp/task/<session>/… (adapter/in/mcpsession).
  2. Tool resolves the session's taskA session-scoped tool in application/tooling looks up the session through SessionRepository and finds its ticket.
  3. Use case runsplanning.Service validates the status (domain TicketStatus) and checks the ticket exists, returning a coded error if not.
  4. Persist through a driven portTicketRepository.Update, implemented by adapter/out/persistence/sqlite.
  5. AnnounceUnder ticketMu, the service hands the change to TicketAnnouncer; orchestration's feed puts a ProjectChange on the project stream.
  6. Clients updatehttpapi streams it over SSE; the browser's tasks module and tui-client's live package apply it. No refresh.

08Where new code goes

I need to…Put it in
Add a concept or a rule about itinternal/domain, as a type or method on the type
Add a use caseThe owning context's service in internal/application/<ctx>; expose it on a driving port in internal/ports
Talk to a new external systemA driven port in internal/ports, an adapter in internal/adapter/out/<tech>, bound in internal/app
React to something another context didSubscribe to its domain event in your context's Subscribe(bus); never import its package
Read another context's dataA narrow read port it already satisfies (CapabilityReader, TicketReader)
Expose it over HTTP / MCPA handler in adapter/in/httpapi or a tool in application/tooling + adapter/in/mcp(session)
Show it in the browserA templ page in adapter/in/web/<page> and a module in web/src/modules/<module>
Make it work in tui-client tooImplement the driving port in adapter/out/httpclient and run the portstest suite against it
